title: vpc-peering-blackhole-handoff-notes
content:
Summary:

This is a lightweight incident review + handoff notes for the VPC peering blackhole event that impacted the private control-plane reachability for customer clusters in eu-west-1 on 2026-03-09. The primary symptoms were sporadic API timeouts from Private control plane to agent heartbeats, escalating 504s for control-plane RPCs, and failed health-checks for on-prem customer tunnels. Impact window ~2026-03-09 03:12 to 2026-03-09 04:07 UTC.

High-level impact:
- Number of affected customers: 6 (private deployments using peered VPCs in eu-west-1)
- Visible symptoms: agent heartbeat gaps, config sync failures, control-plane API 504s, degraded monitoring dataplane for those customers.
- Customer-visible downtime: intermittent failures; majority of traffic returned once alternate peering was routed.

Initial detection and alerting:
- 03:12 UTC: SRE synthetic control-plane ping alarm (5xx ratio) fired (pager escalated to on-call).
- 03:15 UTC: Internal Slack channel #sre-private notified via pager; on-call initiated war room.
- 03:18 UTC: Multiple private deployment customers reported increased error rates to CS.

Timeline (reconstructed):
- 03:10 UTC: BGP flaps reported on cloud-provider peering fabric (automated BGP telemetry).
- 03:12 UTC: Synthetic control-plane check crosses threshold -> initial pager.
- 03:16 UTC: Observed asymmetric flow traces for peering connection between our VPC (10.5.0.0/16) and customer VPCs (172.31.0.0/16) showing traffic blackhole at cloud peering fabric.
- 03:23 UTC: Engineering rotated routes to secondary interconnect (manual route injection via private-deployments network rung).
- 03:29 UTC: Control-plane RTTs improved for majority; a subset of customers still showed heartbeat gaps.
- 03:45 UTC: Cloud provider confirmed partial fabric degradation in eu-west-1 peering plane, with 1 of 3 peering switches overloaded.
- 04:07 UTC: Full traffic switched to secondary interconnect; monitoring normalized.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Immediate cause: transient peering fabric overload at the provider that caused selective blackholing of established flows (likely kernel/TCAM table thrash on peering switch).
- Contributing factors: our single primary peering path for those customers (insufficient cross-connect redundancy), lack of automated diversion to secondary interconnect for this specific route map, and a conservative retransmission/heartbeat backoff in agent-side code that amplified perceived downtime.

Telemetry and evidence collected:
- Packet captures from bastion -> customer tunnel showing SYNs leaving but no ACKs returned between 03:11–03:24 UTC.
- BGP chat logs (provider) showing route withdrawal and re-announcement events correlated to overloaded switch timestamps.
- Control-plane logs: spike in RPC timeouts and 502/504 errors.
- Agent-side metrics: heartbeat_missing_count spiked from 0.2/min to 8/min for affected clusters.
- Dashboard snapshot: per-route token-latency and per-tenant error rates (attached in linked artifacts).

Mitigation timeline (what we did):
- 03:20 UTC: Disabled aggressive prefix aggregation that favored the primary peering path and started advertising more specific prefixes to encourage alternate ECMP paths.
- 03:23 UTC: Manual route injection to secondary interconnect (engineer: Miguel).
- 03:27 UTC: Temporary throttle on control-plane background syncs (reducing load on the fabric).
- 04:07 UTC: Verified stabilization and re-enabled standard route aggregation and sync cadence.

Customer communication and handoff:
- CS notified customer technical contacts at 03:30 UTC with preliminary impact summary.
- Public post-incident notification draft prepared (ticket JIRA-INC-4821).
- Handoff to weekday on-call team at 06:00 UTC with action items below.

Near-term action items (owners and ETA):
- Create automated failover play (runbook): a scripted route injection + traffic shifting that can be run from SRE runbook console. Owner: Priya Menon. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- Increase proactive BGP export granularity for customer peering to allow graceful ECMP when primary fabric shows abnormal loss. Owner: Network infra. ETA: 2026-04-05.
- Quick fix: add health check to route-controller to detect >3s blackhole windows and auto-trigger secondary interconnect. Owner: Samir Banerjee. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Agent change: add jitter to heartbeat backoff and fallback sooner to cached control-plane endpoints. Owner: infra/agents team. ETA: 2026-04-08.

Longer-term engineering changes:
- Formal multi-path design for Private/VPC peering in eu-west-1 with at least two independent fabric paths and automated failover. (Coord with cloud provider partner).
- Add synthetic checks per-tenant across both interconnects and add anomaly detection for asymmetric flows.
- Post-incident runbook: include explicit triage steps for peering blackholes (what logs to capture, which provider APIs to query, and fallback commands).

Runbook draft excerpts (commands & quick checks):
1) Verify symptoms:
   - curl -sv --max-time 5 https://private-controlplane.<tenant>.redwood.internal/health
   - tcpdump -ni eth0 host <customer-peer-ip> and look for SYNs w/out ACKs
2) Provider checks:
   - check BGP session status via provider CLI/API (bgp-session show <peering-id>)
   - fetch provider peering telemetry: provider.api/peering/<peering-id>/events
3) Remediation steps (manual):
   - inject specific routes: infra-tool route inject --prefix <customer-prefix> --next-hop secondary-interconnect
   - temporarily reduce control-plane syncs: curl -XPOST https://runbook-api/ops/scale-down-syncs
4) Post-fix verification:
   - confirm agent heartbeats restored for 5 consecutive minutes
   - monitor control-plane RPC 95th pct latency < 250ms for 10m window

Open questions (for RCA):
- Why did the provider fabric route-restore not automatically rebalance flows to healthy switches? (provider follow-up ongoing)
- Could our aggregated route advertisement have masked visibility into per-tenant path health?
- Do we need shorter detection windows for peering blackholes to avoid long heartbeat backoffs?

Communication artifacts to prepare:
- Short incident summary for affected customers (CS to send): one-paragraph root cause + ETA for preventative measures. Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- Internal postmortem document (consolidate telemetry, full timeline, and RCA) to be published to SRE Confluence. Owner: Anika. ETA: 2026-03-22.

Appendix: immediate notes for the on-call taking over:
- Retain packet captures from bastion (s3://private-deployments/pcaps/2026-03-09-peering-blackhole.pcap)
- Watch for recurring SYN-only windows in the next 72 hours. Set a temporary alert: heartbeat_missing_count > 3/min for > 10 minutes.
- If blackhole recurs, escalate to provider NOC immediately with trace-id from provider telemetry and request switch-level TCAM drain.

If you pick this up for follow-up, please add updates to this doc (append to the bottom) and update the JIRA ticket linked above.

End of notes.
